coordinate_policy.reason: DATA260703 and DATA260708 do not share a guaranteed identical Motive world-to-table relationship. Without table anchors in DATA260703, using DATA260708 to infer the old transform would be underconstrained and not precise enough.

competition_table_frame.origin: table:Marker 001, P1/liang-side left corner on the tabletop
competition_table_frame.axis_definition: X points from P1/liang to P2, Y positive points to P1's left so the P1 right corner has negative Y, Z points upward and tabletop height is 0.

datasets.reason: processed old data exists, but no valid per-take table anchor/rigid body calibration was found; DATA260708 transform must not be reused for it
recommended_use: stroke-type and motion-pattern analysis in local/body-relative coordinates
algorithm prototyping that does not require landing/success/table-side labels

racket_reference_point.racket_pos: Motive rigid-body center inside the racket, not the physical ball-contact point on the racket face
racket_reference_point.distance_at_hit_m: ball center to racket rigid-body center distance; nonzero contact distance is expected

notes: gao and liang are player skeletons; gao01 and liang01 are their rackets
competition table frame uses Marker001 as origin, Marker002 as P2-left, Marker003 as P2-right, and Marker004 as P1-right
DATA260708_train_table.npz is retained as an earlier marker-estimated local frame and should not be treated as the final competition frame
recommended labeled dataset uses a longer -0.6 s to +1.0 s hit-centered window for landing/success labeling
success labels are reliable only for samples with a detected post-hit table bounce inside the sample window
racket_pos is the internal racket rigid-body center, so ball-racket distance at hit is not expected to be zero
ball trajectory is reconstructed from Unlabeled markers with same-id continuity and +1/+2 id-jump preference
non-rule id links are retained only when motion continuity passes the configured thresholds and should remain auditable
